In Elsinore, a Radiant Andrew Scott Finds Life in a Play About Death

Contracting HIV is no longer a death sentence. But before the current medications and treatments emerged, the AIDS crisis of the 1980s and 1990s touched almost everyone, gay or straight, whether you wanted to admit it or not. Friends of friends, acquaintances or associates who brightened your day, or, worst of all, a loved one: people you cherished could wither and disappear in practically a heartbeat.
